clue.text: Courteousness from old man initially in Leeds, say

indicators.note: in places the old-man letters within the Leeds example

parts.note: Leeds is an example of a city

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word man

explanation.surface: Politeness shown by an elderly gentleman from the Yorkshire city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' looks like the familiar OM, but 'initially' applies only to 'man': O plus M goes inside CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Comity is mutual civility and considerate behaviour, a formal word for courteousness.

clue.text: Be in cold and horribly damp temporary overnight facility

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: in puts the word Be inside the rearranged letters
horribly suggests the word damp is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to sleep somewhere chilly and unpleasantly wet for a night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be' reads as a verb in the surface, but it is just the two letters, which 'in' places within AMPD, the jumble made by 'horribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp bed is a folding bed put up for a guest or a night away, a makeshift sleeping arrangement.

clue.text: I'm Norma: rely on being transformed into famous actress

indicators.note: being transformed tells us the letters of the quoted phrase are changed into another form

explanation.surface: Norma Jeane speaking, relying on a transformation to become a star.
explanation.walkthrough: Marilyn Monroe was born Norma Jeane, so the woman speaking in the surface really is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marilyn Monroe was a Hollywood star of the 1950s, about as famous as screen actresses get.

clue.text: Somehow he's best, keen, full of energy — wonderful person

indicators.note: full of means the anagrammed letters hold the energy letter inside
somehow signals the letters of he's best, keen are arranged in some other way

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Praise for an eager, energetic person who is simply the best.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator rearranges HESBESTKEEN, and 'full of' adds E to make the twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The bee's knees is an idiom for someone or something outstandingly excellent.

clue.text: Sink getting old food

parts.note: to sink or droop is to sag

explanation.surface: A kitchen sink with stale food in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy foodstuff from palm pith, often made into a milk pudding.

clue.text: A paper given time has info processed somehow

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
an era is a period of time

indicators.note: processed means the letters of has info are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A newspaper given time processes its information in some odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: The last word looks like an anagram signal but is the definition; 'processed' does the work, turning HASINFO into FASHION.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something after a fashion means doing it in some way or other, not very well: roughly, somehow.

clue.text: Chore mixing paint?

definitions.note: the question mark admits ochre is strictly a pigment used in paint

indicators.note: mixing tells us the letters of Chore are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Is mixing paint a tedious household job?
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used for colouring paints.

clue.text: Some smashes for a Wimbledon champion

indicators.note: some means only part of the word smashes is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Tennis smashes good enough for a Wimbledon winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Ashe won the Wimbledon men's singles title in 1975.

clue.text: Number working in a theatre

parts.note: read number as one who numbs: a person deadening sensation in an operating theatre

explanation.surface: A musical number performed on a theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song or routine, but it is NUMB-er, one who numbs, and the theatre is a hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist doctor numbs patients by giving drugs before and during surgery.

clue.text: Certain mammals — planet contains five pairs perhaps

indicators.note: contains has the planet holding the number inside it

parts.note: Mars is a planet
five pairs make ten

explanation.surface: Odd zoology: a planet holding animals in five pairs, Noah-style.
explanation.definitionFit: Martens are slender weasel-like carnivores of the forest, a group of mammals.

clue.text: Nick has no time to go to church

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick is too busy to attend church.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads as a man's name, but it is a small cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A nick and a notch are both small V-shaped cuts in an edge.

clue.text: Be levered somehow into building high up?

indicators.note: somehow signals the letters of Be levered are put together some other way

explanation.surface: Being levered into a lofty building, perhaps with a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a summerhouse or turret placed on a height to command a fine view.

clue.text: Feel bad about street in Paris

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to regret it

explanation.definitionFit: Rue means to regret bitterly, and is also the ordinary French word for a road in a town.

clue.text: European to rush around part of UK

indicators.note: around means the rushing word goes round the UK region

parts.note: to dash is to rush
NI is Northern Ireland, part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A European hurrying round a corner of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane, or Danish person, comes from Denmark, a European country.

clue.text: Groups of schoolteachers maybe in English county

definitions.meaning: the bodies of employees of organisations such as schools
The usual abbreviation of Staffordshire, a county in the English Midlands

explanation.definitionFit: A school's teachers form its staff; Staffs is the short name for the county of Staffordshire.

clue.text: Hesitation to put launch onto loch

indicators.note: onto in a down clue puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: to shy is to throw or launch something
Ness is the famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Reluctance to launch a boat on a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launch' suggests a boat, but here it means to throw; a coconut shy is a throwing game.
explanation.definitionFit: Shyness is timidity that holds a person back, a form of hesitation.

clue.text: Mucky stuff pleasant? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means the synonym is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: good means pleasant

explanation.surface: Is a mucky substance pleasant? Only partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Goo is any sticky, slimy or messy substance.

clue.text: Greek character in school with arts degree

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: A Greek pupil at school who also holds an arts degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests a place of learning, but a gam is a school of whales, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is the third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Fresh source of milk in part of America

parts.note: fresh means new
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cow

explanation.surface: Fresh dairy produced in a region of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: New Jersey is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Sport is conflict with referee finally intervening

indicators.note: intervening means the letter comes between letters of the conflict word

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of referee

explanation.surface: Sport turns into a war when the referee finally steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' looks like a game, but it is the verb: to sport a hat is to wear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport clothing is to wear it showily.

clue.text: Join in swimming finally in lake

indicators.note: in places the closing letter inside the lake word

parts.note: a mere is a lake

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of swimming

explanation.surface: An invitation to join others swimming in a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge is to combine or come together into one.

clue.text: Very stupid and insane possibly — one must be kept in

indicators.note: must be kept in means the numeral sits inside the rearranged letters
possibly signals another arrangement of the letters of insane

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone foolish and maybe mad has to be confined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns INSANE into ASINNE, and 'must be kept in' places I between the two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish to an extreme, literally like an ass.

clue.text: Cuts lines on graph?

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means cuts or scraps, as in budget ...
the plural of axis, the reference lines of a graph

explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut or chop; axes is also the plural of axis, the reference lines on a chart.

clue.text: Gems of quality brought aboard ship

indicators.note: brought aboard puts the quality word inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
tone is a quality of sound or character

explanation.surface: Fine gems are carried onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious stones is another name for gems.
